arguments.content:
# Fair-housing audit memo — seller's book (RE-FH-9)

**Standard applied:** RE-FH-9 (Real-estate marketing collateral fair-housing standard), including the 2026 amendments at §5. The inventory audited is `seller_book_sections.csv` (30 sections, SEC-01–SEC-30). The audit was run against the standard as amended, not against the standing disclosure paragraph the book happens to carry, per §5a.

**Deliverables:** `fairhousing_audit.csv` (one row per section, in inventory order), `results.json` (sign-off counts). This memo is the reasoning behind them.

---

## Rules applied (as amended)

1. **Personal-narrative solicitation (§1).** Any section that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, **whatever its role**.

2. **Protected-class language (§2).** A section naming a protected-class term — or a proxy for one — is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`. Protected classes: race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status. Proxies count: houses of worship, parish/faith schools, and describing a street/area by the kind of household that lives on it (reaches familial status and religion).

3. **Mandated-disclosure exception (§3).** The disclosure notice is exempt from §2 **only if it names every class the disclosure is required to name** (the full amended list — see §5a). An **abridged** notice (some but not all required classes) earns **no exemption at all**, so the protected-class words inside that defective notice themselves count toward §2. The exemption covers the notice text only; protected-class terms a section uses in its own prose, outside the notice, are never covered. The exemption is from §2 only; every other rule still applies.

4. **Required disclaimer (§4).** Sections in a role responsible for carrying the disclosure must carry a **compliant** notice (naming every required class). A responsible section carrying no notice, or an abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Responsible roles: `closing_page` (§4), and `agent_bio` (per the 2026 amendment 5b). All other roles are not assessed under §4.

5. **2026 amendments (§5).**
   - **5a —** The required disclosure must now also name **marital status** and **source of income** in addition to the §2 list. The full required list is therefore 11 classes: race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, marital status, source of income. A notice omitting either of the two new classes is abridged for the purposes of §3 and §4.
   - **5b —** `agent_bio` sections are now in scope for §4 and carry the same disclaimer responsibility as `closing_page`.

Where §5 conflicts with the earlier sections, §5 governs.

---

## Headline numbers (see `results.json`)

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| `section_count` | 30 |
| `flagged_count` (finding ≠ `none`) | 22 |
| `personal_narrative_count` | 7 |
| `protected_lang_count` | 14 |
| `disclaimer_missing_count` | 11 |

Counts are of **sections**, not labels: a section carrying more than one label is counted once per metric but appears in each label's count.

---

## Findings by rule

### `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` — 7 sections
SEC-02, SEC-07, SEC-08, SEC-17, SEC-24, SEC-27, SEC-29.

Each of these solicits a buyer personal narrative tied to identity, in language such as "write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home would mean to you" (SEC-02, SEC-24), "send a personal note about yourself along with the offer; the one that moves us most is the one we will take" (SEC-07, SEC-27), "we invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves" (SEC-08, SEC-29), or "include a covering letter introducing yourself — the sellers would like to know who is buying" (SEC-17). §1 applies regardless of role, so this finding attaches to `seller_letter`, `closing_page`, `disclosure_block` and `agent_bio` sections alike.

### `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` — 14 sections
SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-17, SEC-19, SEC-22, SEC-23, SEC-25.

Two distinct mechanisms produce this finding:

**A. Protected-class proxies in the section's own prose (6 sections).** These are flagged on the body text itself, which §3 never covers:
- SEC-03 and SEC-19 — "a quiet, **family-oriented street**… with two **churches**… and a well-regarded **parish school**" (familial status + religion proxies).
- SEC-07 and SEC-25 — "the block suits **churchgoing households** and has kept the long-established **families** who built it" (religion + familial status).
- SEC-09 — "popular with **young families**; the **parish hall** runs a toddler group" (familial status + religion).
- SEC-17 — "a **congregation-centred** neighbourhood where most households have been in the same **faith community**" (religion).

**B. Abridged disclosure notices (8 sections).** These sections carry a disclosure notice that names some but not all of the 11 required classes, so under §3 they earn no §2 exemption and the protected-class terms inside the notice count. All of these notices still name §2 classes (race, religion, etc.), so each is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`:
- SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-23 — notice names the original nine classes but omits **marital status** and **source of income** (abridged per 5a).
- SEC-15 — notice names only "race, color, religion or sex".
- SEC-16 — notice names only "race, color, religion, sex or familial status".
- SEC-22 — notice names only "race, color, religion, sex, familial status or national origin".

Note the consequence intended by §3: a defective notice does not merely fail the disclaimer rule — it actively converts the disclosure's own protected-class words into a §2 violation. Six of these (SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-23) are also `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`; SEC-04 and SEC-22 are `disclosure_block` sections, which are not §4-responsible, so they carry only the §2 finding.

### `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` — 11 sections
SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-21, SEC-23, SEC-30.

All are in a §4-responsible role (`closing_page` or, per 5b, `agent_bio`) and carry either no notice or an abridged one:
- **No notice at all:** SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-21, SEC-30.
- **Abridged notice** (missing marital status/source of income, or more): SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-23.

`disclosure_block` sections (SEC-04, SEC-08, SEC-22) are not §4-responsible and are not assessed here, even where their notice is abridged (SEC-04, SEC-22 are still caught by §2, above). `listing_copy` and `seller_letter` sections are not §4-responsible.

---

## Sections that passed (8)
SEC-01, SEC-06, SEC-10, SEC-13, SEC-18, SEC-20, SEC-26, SEC-28. Each is either non-responsible role copy with no protected-class language, or a responsible-role section carrying the full 11-class notice with clean body text (SEC-10, SEC-13, SEC-26, SEC-28).

---

## Why the standing disclosure paragraph is the dominant issue
The pre-amendment disclosure paragraph in circulation names the original nine classes but omits **marital status** and **source of income**. It appears, unchanged, in SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14 and SEC-23, and is the single reason those sections fail both §3 (so they become `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`) and, where §4 applies, §4 (`DISCLAIMER_MISSING`). Per §5a, the book must be audited against the amended list regardless of the template's currency. Reissuing the notice paragraph to include "marital status" and "source of income" — as the compliant notices in SEC-08, SEC-10, SEC-13, SEC-19, SEC-24, SEC-26, SEC-28 and SEC-29 already do — would clear the disclaimer failures and the §2-by-abridged-notice failures in one pass, provided the surrounding body text is also cleaned of the proxy language and the personal-narrative solicitations identified above.

## Recommendation for sign-off
The book is **not** compliant as drafted. 22 of 30 sections carry at least one finding. The blocking issues for print are the 7 personal-narrative solicitations (§1, which no notice can cure) and the abridged/absent disclaimers on the 11 responsible-role sections; the proxy language in the descriptive copy is a further §2 exposure. Until these are remediated, RE-FH-9 cannot be signed off.
